Agreement.Title: Articles of Enrolment
Agreement.FormNumber: FORM 1-B — ARTICLES OF ENROLMENT AND GENERAL CONSENTS
Agreement.Intro: Before anything else, the Directorate requires your agreement to the terms below. Recruits are advised to read them in full.
Agreement.ReadingTime: Estimated reading time: {time}. Recruits are advised to allow sufficient time.

Page1.Title: Induction
Page1.Intro1: The letter said to report here. This is here — a Directorate terminal, humming quietly, waiting for a name it doesn't have yet.
Page1.Intro2: You're about to build the character you'll be playing. This takes most people twenty to thirty minutes. Nothing here is final — anything too complicated for a form gets finished properly once you're actually in the game, on your character's own sheet.
Page1.WhatToExpect: You'll choose who your character is — their ancestry, their background, their training — and answer a handful of real questions about who they are as a person, not just what they can do. If a question ever seems unclear, look for a small toggle that switches the form to plain, out-of-character language explaining exactly what's being asked. Every answer here feeds directly into the campaign; nothing is just flavour text. At the end, you'll have a working character and a token waiting for you at the table.
Page1.WhatYouNeed: Just a concept — a rough idea of who you want to play. Everything else, this form will ask you for, one step at a time.

Page2.PickPrompt: Pick an ancestry from the list to see what it gives you. You can switch as often as you like.
Page2.Title: Ancestry
Page2.Intro: Your character's real ancestry — not the one they'll wear at the table. Every option here is real and mechanical; how it's disguised in play is entirely yours to decide later.
Page2.LoadFailedBody: That's this terminal's fault, not yours — nothing was lost. Use Back below, then Begin again; if it keeps happening, tell your GM.
Page2.HelpBody: Ancestry permanently sets six things on your sheet: two or three ability boosts (and sometimes one flaw), your base Hit Points, your Size, your Speed, and which languages you start with. It does not pick an ancestry feat — you'll choose one on your own character sheet once your token is on the table, the same way class feats work.
Page2.LockdownNote: Playing something other than Human, Elf, Dwarf, Gnome or Halfling is fully encouraged — it just means a few extra private questions later in the process. Those are between you and this screen; whether you ever tell anyone at the table is entirely your call, and there is no wrong answer.

Page3.PickPrompt: Pick a background from the list to see what it gives you. You can switch as often as you like.
Page3.Title: Background
Page3.Intro: Who your character was before the letter arrived. Every background is real and mechanical, same as ancestry — search or browse the full list below.
Page3.SkillsSeeDescription: This background's exact skill grant is a little unusual — see the description above for the real wording.
Page3.HelpBody: Background permanently sets three things on your sheet: two ability boosts, training in one or two skills (often including a Lore skill), and a skill feat. It does not pick the skill feat for you — you'll choose it on your own character sheet once your token is on the table, the same way ancestry and class feats work. A few backgrounds phrase their skill grant as a real choice ("Crafting or Piloting"); when that happens, the description above is the actual rule, not the summary rows below it.

Page4.PickPrompt: Pick a class to see its training, defences and key ability.
Page4.Title: Class
Page4.Intro: The training your character actually received. Only six real specialisations exist — pick one below.
Page4.PlusMoreSkills: Plus {count} more skills of your choice — pick them on your own character sheet once your token is on the table.
Page4.HelpBody: Class permanently sets your key ability (the one every class feature and most of your best rolls key off), your Hit Points per level, starting Perception and saving-throw proficiencies, and your starting weapon/armor training. It does not pick your class features, feats or spells — those come next, on your own character sheet, once your token is on the table. Your Class DC starts Trained, same as every class at level 1.

Page5.Title: Attribute Boosts
Page5.Intro: Pick four different attributes to raise, on top of what your ancestry, background and class already gave you. The number beside each shows where it will end up.
Page5.TallyLabel: Your six attributes and where each one ends up
Page5.HelpBody: This permanently raises one of the six numbers that drive almost every roll you make — the single most consequential page in this form. A free boost can land on an ability your ancestry, background or class already raised; it simply adds another +1 there. The four you pick here must all be different from each other, but can repeat what's already been set elsewhere.

Page6.Title: Portrait
Page6.Intro: A photograph for your file — optional, but every character in this campaign uses the same frame, and it's a nice thing to have waiting for you at the table. Upload one below and adjust it to fit; Section Nine keeps standard imagery on hand for anyone who'd rather skip this.
Page6.ViewportLabel: Photo crop. Drag, or use the arrow keys, to move the photo; + and − zoom.
Page6.CropHint: Drag the photo to move it. The zoom slider, the mouse wheel, or + and − zoom in and out.
Page6.InvalidFileType: That doesn't look like an image file — choose a photo (JPEG, PNG, WebP, etc.) instead.
Page6.FileTooLarge: That file is too large (over 20MB). Try a smaller photo.
Page6.HelpBody: There's no mechanical effect from your choice of photo, or from skipping it entirely. Every character portrait in this campaign is shown in the same tall frame, so keeping the crop close to the guide box just keeps your character looking consistent next to the rest of the cast once play begins.

Page7.Title: Finishing Details
Page7.Intro: The mechanical parts are done. This page is short answers only — one line each, nothing that needs thinking about for long. Every box has a row of suggestions you can click to fill it in fast, and every box is also just a box: write whatever you like instead, or as well. All of it lands on your real character sheet.
Page7.OptionalNote: None of this is required except your name — write as much or as little as you like.

Page8.Title: Personal Declaration
Page8.Intro: Four questions, and a box for everything they didn't ask. Every answer becomes something the campaign actually uses — a person who can come back, a side plot, a vulnerability, a reason to be here. Write as much as you want; there is no length these boxes are expecting.
Page8.OptionalNote: Nothing on this page is required. Leave any or all of it blank and continue — you can always come back to this later.

PagePlayer.Title: A Page for the Player
PagePlayer.FormNumber: OUT OF CHARACTER — FOR THE PLAYER
PagePlayer.Intro: This page is for you, the person playing, not for your character. The campaign is being built around what the six of you enjoy, so this is the place to say what a good game looks like to you: what you like, what you don't, and what you'd like to do.
PagePlayer.OptionalNote: Nothing on this page is required, and none of it is a test. Answer what you like and leave the rest. Your GM reads your answers; the other players don't.

Page9.Title: Review & Confirm
Page9.Intro: Everything below is what actually gets written down. Nothing is created until you confirm.
Page9.ConfirmNote: Class feats, spells, an ancestry/background feat, and any skills beyond what's listed above still need finishing on your own character sheet, once your token is on the table — same as every real character.
Page9.SuccessTitle: Done. You're in the system now.
Page9.SuccessBody: {actorName} exists, and your token is already waiting on the landing scene. Finish the rest — feats, spells, the last few skills — on your own character sheet.

Demo.Title: Demo Walkthroughs
Demo.Intro: Every step here is a real action against this real world — nothing is mocked. If a step breaks, that's the point: something drifted, and it's better to find out here than at the table.

SessionIntegration.Title: Session 0/1: Scene Runner, the map, and the stage
SessionIntegration.Step1: Open Episode One and land on its first scene, The Road In.
SessionIntegration.Step2: Cue the next beat, Kit Issue — one click, since it now both loads the script and cuts the table there. Kit Issue is a different location, so watch the party's marker cross the map before the scene changes underneath it.
SessionIntegration.Step3: Bring Kit Issue's quartermaster, Nobu, onto the stage. His brief calls for an Announced entrance, so the banner should sound on its own — nobody has to remember to click it.
SessionIntegration.Step4: Same idea again, a second time: cue Canteen, proving the map crossing isn't a one-off tied to a single pair of locations.
SessionIntegration.Step5: Bring Canteen's Taka onto the stage. Her brief calls for the loudest tier there is — Splash — and it should fire automatically too.
SessionIntegration.Step6: Open the Sound Desk directly from the Deck's own Sound pill — the Deck should no longer be blind to what's playing.

RoadInTravel.Title: The Road In → Intake Medicals: six candidates, one map crossing
RoadInTravel.Step1: Scatter six temporary candidate tokens across the mainland — six different starting lives, nowhere near the fortress island yet.
RoadInTravel.Step2: Open Episode One and land on its first scene, The Road In.
RoadInTravel.Step3: Watch all six candidates actually travel — each its own real, separately-routed journey at its own real pace — converging on Candidate Gate.
RoadInTravel.Step4: Cue the very next beat, Intake Medicals — watch the party's own marker cross the real map, calibrated against the hub's own real Tiles, before the scene changes underneath it.

Hint.polygon: Click each corner · double-click or Enter finishes · Esc cancels · Backspace undoes a point · hold Shift to turn angle snap off
Hint.circle: Drag from the centre out to the edge
Hint.bisect: Click a cut line across the loaded region, both ends on or past its border · Enter finishes

Story.Pending: {count} placement(s) saved here, waiting for "npm run locations" to apply them.
Story.Armed: Click the building or pin on the map where "{label}" happens. Shift-click picks the area instead. Esc cancels.
Story.AlsoMove: These agree with it today. Move them too:
Story.WhyHere: Why here? (optional; replaces the old reasoning)
Story.DrawingFor: Drawing a place for "{label}". Draw it, name it, Save; then confirm it on the Story tab.
Story.NotDrawable: That place has no outline on this map to show.
Story.NothingThere: Nothing there to place it at. Click a building, a pin or an area.
Story.Saved: {count} placement(s) saved. Pull with "npm run locations" to apply them to the scenes.

Published.Heading: On the map already
Published.Failed: Could not load the existing locations -- see the console.
Published.NoHub: There is no Campaign Map scene to lay the existing locations on.
Published.NotThisScene: Open the Campaign Map scene to see them.
Published.NothingToFit: There is nothing on the map to show.
Published.SomeFailed: {count} location file(s) had no outline to draw.

LocationEditor.NoItems: Nothing drawn yet -- pick a tool above and draw on the Campaign Map.
LocationEditor.Close: Close (the real location is not deleted)
LocationEditor.NothingChanged: Nothing has changed on that location, so there is nothing to save.
LocationEditor.NotYetSaved: not yet saved to the repo
LocationEditor.SelectExactlyOne: Select exactly one item to edit its details -- several are selected right now.

Bisect.Prompt: Type the real, already-promoted region's own id to load it for cutting.
Bisect.NotARegion: "{id}" is not a region -- only a region can be bisected.
Bisect.NoGeometry: "{id}" has no derived geometry to cut -- resync it first.
Bisect.NoTarget: Load a region to bisect first.
Bisect.BadCut: That cut meets the region's border {count} time(s); a split needs exactly two. Draw it again, ends on or past the border.
Bisect.Saved: Queued a split of "{id}". Pull with "npm run locations" to actually cut it.

Advice.Orphaned: Written, but not required until a deeper depth:
Advice.DepthOk: Meets everything its declared depth requires.

Field.Name: Name
Field.Note: Note -- the rough brief this was drawn from (required)

LocationEditor.PendingCount: {0} not yet pulled into the repo
LocationEditor.NothingSelected: Select or draw an item first.
LocationEditor.NoteRequired: A note is required -- what is this, roughly?
LocationEditor.SavedNew: Saved. Pull with "npm run locations" to promote it into a real location file.
